structured_output.reasoning: The incident quote ("I told you to leave the formatter alone, and it was changed") is one of the three evidence items the remedy was directly built from, and the remedy text explicitly cites "don't touch the formatter" as its lead example. The remedy instructs the agent to treat user-stated mid-task constraints as durable boundaries and to check every planned action against them before proceeding, stopping to ask rather than silently overriding — which directly targets the exact failure mode shown here (violating an explicit "leave X alone" instruction while continuing the broader task). Dedup checks against R1-R5 correctly show no overlap, since those govern verification-before-claiming-done and destructive-action confirmation, not scope-constraint adherence. The remedy is a standing behavioral instruction rather than a mechanically enforced hook, so there's some residual reliance on the agent actually re-checking constraints each turn, but that's an inherent limitation of claude-md-style fixes for ad hoc, conversation-declared constraints (as the routing rationale reasonably explains) — not a gap in this remedy's applicability to the incident itself.
